claims.head: Something has to give
claims.body: The Rangers are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Hurricanes are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Rangers’ power play wins out. Oliver Bjorkstrand is out 2-3 months (upper body injury), reported after he played in their last game.

Sean Durzi is day to day and has missed the last 8 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Braden Schneider has taken his spot beside Marcus Pettersson. That pair has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 117:15 together, up from 45% with Durzi.
Glenn Gawdin was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside Eeli Tolvanen and Jaroslav Chmelař.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

story.head: Something has to give
paras: The Rangers have won three straight, while the Hurricanes (16-3-3) lost 2-1 in overtime to Montréal on Thursday. The Canes played last night, and the Rangers are rested. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Hurricanes first (third in the NHL) and the Rangers third (tied for 12th).
This season, the Rangers have outscored teams 67-58, but only 42-40 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 15-9.

The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd), so the Rangers could find some good looks against them. Carolina has scored 4.00 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.18, the second fewest. On the other side, the Rangers lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest), get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Rangers’ power play against the Hurricanes’ penalty killers is strength against strength.

Sebastian Aho (12 G / 17 A / 29 P in 22 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Andrei Svechnikov (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind, with seven points in his last five games. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (2 G / 22 A / 24 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Alexis Lafrenière (10 G / 12 A / 22 P in 22 GP) has a team-high ten goals.
Brandon Bussi (4-2-2 / .872 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for Carolina, and Dylan Garand (7-7-1 / .910 SV% in 13 GS) for the Rangers.
At home, Mike Sullivan likes to send Cuylle, Miller and Kartye out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov.

items.text: J.T. Miller is two assists from 500.
Nikolaj Ehlers has a point in six straight games against the Rangers.
The Rangers are newly without Pavel Dorofeyev and Oliver Bjorkstrand, and have been without Igor Shesterkin and Sean Durzi for several games. Dylan Garand is expected to start.
William Carrier has one goal on chances worth about 5.1 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
